gaps.sentence: They behaved ___ nothing at all had happened.
gaps.explanation: 'As if + past perfect' signals that the comparison is contrary to fact.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.

gaps.sentence: No sooner had the applause died ___ the encore began.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner... than' is invariable; 'when' would be wrong here.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.

gaps.sentence: She took an evening job ___ fund her law degree.
gaps.explanation: 'In order to' + bare infinitive expresses purpose after a noun phrase subject.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that the road was icy, the bus kept its usual speed.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that + clause' concedes a full clause after a preposition.
